SUNeVision.why: Hong Kong colocation operator (iAdvantage) whose revenue grows as US and Chinese hyperscale and AI customers take high-density capacity for AI-driven deployments (MEGA IDC, liquid cooling).
SUNeVision.evidence: SUNeVision operates its data centre business under the iAdvantage brand ... Demand has been driven by both international and Chinese hyperscale customers, with the latter especially increasingly seeking large-scale deployments to support AI-driven workloads. ... We are privileged to already serve basically all top US and Chinese cloud and AI companies.

players.product: Hong Kong carrier-neutral colocation data centres (iAdvantage MEGA Campus: MEGA-i connectivity hub, MEGA IDC high-density, liquid-cooling-ready AI campus)

quarterly_data.quarter: SUNeVision press release: Final Results Announcement for the Year Ended 30 June 2026 (09-01-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: FY2026 (year ended 30 June 2026) results: recurring revenue from data centre and IT facilities grew 8% to HK$2,856 million, supported by newly commissioned facilities and organic growth; total revenue grew 6% year-on-year to HK$3,117 million; EBITDA rose 8% to HK$2,300 million with margins expanding from 72% to 74%; profit attributable to owners up 17% to HK$1,146 million (helped by lower borrowing costs).
quarterly_data.figure: recurring data centre revenue HK$2,856 million (+8%); total revenue HK$3,117 million (+6%); EBITDA HK$2,300 million (+8%), margin 72% to 74%; profit HK$1,146 million (+17%)

quarterly_data.quarter: SUNeVision press release: Final Results Announcement for the Year Ended 30 June 2026 (09-01-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Chairman Kwok Ping-luen, Raymond: demand for premium data centre infrastructure in Hong Kong improved significantly over the year and accelerated meaningfully in the second half, driven by both international and Chinese hyperscale customers, the latter increasingly seeking large-scale deployments to support AI-driven workloads; AI is a major catalyst. 'We are privileged to already serve basically all top US and Chinese cloud and AI companies, and these customers are happy to expand with us.' During the year the company completed renewals with two of its largest customers with strong rental reversion. The company says it prioritises premium, fungible, long-life-cycle deployments and sustainable rents over simply maximising occupancy; while new supply from peers is expected over the medium term, it believes its locations, power availability and connectivity will remain key differentiators.

quarterly_data.quarter: SUNeVision press release: Final Results Announcement for the Year Ended 30 June 2026 (09-01-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Occupancy and market tightness (results announcement): substantial portions of available capacity have been absorbed across the Hong Kong market, leaving premium, high-specification capacity increasingly scarce. MEGA Plus (Tseung Kwan O) is basically fully occupied and channelling new demand to MEGA IDC; MEGA Two (Shatin) remains effectively fully occupied, with revitalisation projects capturing high-density hyperscale and cloud demand; MEGA Fanling (single-user, asset-light) remains fully operational and occupied; MEGA Gateway (Tsuen Wan) has over 90% of its deployed capacity taken up by cloud, telco and banking clients, with an increasing proportion of AI-related deployments.
quarterly_data.figure: MEGA Gateway over 90% of deployed capacity taken up; MEGA Plus and MEGA Two fully occupied

quarterly_data.quarter: SUNeVision press release: Final Results Announcement for the Year Ended 30 June 2026 (09-01-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Contracted backlog and new commitments: transaction price allocated to remaining performance obligations for data centre and IT facilities colocation services was HK$10,921,134,000 at 30 June 2026 (2025: HK$9,031,862,000), of which HK$1,888,924,000 is expected to be recognised within one year. At MEGA IDC Phase One (approximately 500,000 square feet of GFA, 50MW of power), the company secured a major commitment from a single customer (not named) that is expected to increase facility occupancy from approximately 30% to around 70% upon full implementation; the customer is moving in, and the company is finalising negotiations with two hyperscale customers for the remaining two floors of Phase One.
quarterly_data.figure: colocation remaining performance obligations HK$10,921,134,000 (2025: HK$9,031,862,000); MEGA IDC Phase One occupancy approximately 30% to around 70%

quarterly_data.quarter: SUNeVision press release: Final Results Announcement for the Year Ended 30 June 2026 (09-01-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Capacity plan: because of strong demand (some customers ready to pre-commit), the company is accelerating MEGA IDC and will build out the entire Phase Two in one go instead of staggering it into Phase 2a and 2b, with a target ready-for-service date of 2028; Phase Two will provide about 700,000 sq. ft. of premium, high-density data centre space; planning the remaining phases together gives flexibility to accommodate larger-block customer mandates requiring liquid cooling and ultra-high power densities. The integrated development will increase the total GFA of the company's Hong Kong data centres from 2.3 million square feet (30 June 2026) to almost 3 million square feet, and power capacity from 150MW to 280MW.
quarterly_data.figure: Phase Two about 700,000 sq. ft., ready 2028; GFA 2.3 million to almost 3 million square feet; power capacity 150MW to 280MW

quarterly_data.quarter: SUNeVision press release: Final Results Announcement for the Year Ended 30 June 2026 (09-01-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: MEGA-i connectivity hub (results announcement): supports an ecosystem of approximately 15,000 cross-connects for hundreds of carriers, ISPs, enterprises and cloud providers; strategic power upgrades and liquid-cooling solutions have been deployed at the facility to meet rising customer demand. Chairman: Hong Kong is losing competitiveness in subsea cables (12 major subsea cables now versus 21 for Singapore; 11 versus 13 in 2019), and the company is working with the Government and industry to attract more cable landings.

quarterly_data.quarter: SUNeVision press release: Final Results Announcement for the Year Ended 30 June 2026 (09-01-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Customer concentration and capital spending (FY2026 financial statements): the largest two customers (not named), both in the data centre and IT facilities segment, accounted for about 19% and 14% of total revenue (2025: 18% and 14%). Additions to property, plant and equipment in the data centre and IT facilities segment were HK$'000 987,047 (2025: 1,340,496). The company says it runs a demand-driven capital approach and can deliver space within four to six months of order confirmation.
quarterly_data.figure: largest two customers about 19% and 14% of revenue; data centre PP&E additions HK$'000 987,047 (2025: 1,340,496)
